title: AI 2D Animation Generation without spritesheets
author: Lashaa
selftext:
Hey guys,

Past few years, as a solo dev I used to create some mobile games and casino slots, I always had a problem with animations - frame to frame, image to video and then spritesheets was not enough quality even it was perfectly looped. While Spine 2D had a perfect quality, it was always hard for me, never enjoyed and couldn't learn it, and cost of spine artist and the timing of animation creation was super high. This year, in February I started my personal project to generate real skeletal, spine level animations based on AI. 

So, I have created my owned model, and fine-tuned it around 2000 perfectly cut layered psds, and around 3000 spine animations. After each iteration, feedback and fine-tuning again. The idea was: From just one, static png without layers - getting real quality skeletal animations. You can see in the video what I made. Right now my model does:

* Cut the image into the layers
* Rigging
* Animations applied (from pre-defined libraries, 10K+ motion library built).

For physics and IK applying I am using claude opus and gpt astra (planning to train my model for it too). 

Exported animation files are .json, .skel and .atlas, with also its owned .png

For some characters, or symbols, the model works really well, for some pngs, still getting stuck. 

My goal is to continue fine-tuning for cutting layers and animation applying, and then add new things: the most important for me is to let it make custom animations from the prompt, not predefined animations. Second thing for me is to make it fully based on my model for physics and IK. Planning VFX automation too, just not have anything yet, just have some VFX effects which works with predefined animations library, but want it too fully automated based on prompts too, let's see.

Still, the main idea is to get high quality skeletal, procedural animations.

  
I have attached a demo video, just for one of my slot game character, how it cuts and applies 4 random animations. 

  
What do you think guys? what'd be your feedback and recommendations?
